newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Spadel sees 1996 loss due to Alardo charge.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Spadel sees 1996 loss due to Alardo charge.

text.p: Belgian beverage firm Spadel said on Friday it plunged into the red in 1996 due to an exceptional charge of about 169 million Belgian francs linked to Portuguese mineral water bottling unit Empresa das Aguas do Alardo.
Spadel, which had a 1995 group net profit of 128 million francs, said the exceptional charge was aimed at totally writing off Alardo's intrinsic value in its consolidated accounts.

Bottles of Alardo were withdrawn from the shelves in Portugal on March 10 after traces of algae were found in some of them. But Spadel said on March 20 that tests in laboratories had found the water to be clear for consumption and that bottling had restarted.
Spadel said consolidated current pre-tax profit was similar to that of 1995. "However...the exceptional charge...will push the net consolidated result into the red," it said.
Spadel also said it would propose to shareholders to pay an unchanged net dividend of 366 francs, "in view of future prospects".
